vector_name: ASIL-D boundary miss — SPFM just below 99%
discriminates: Tests the ASIL-D threshold boundary from BELOW — 98.08% is just under the 99% ASIL-D target, forcing the calculator to apply strict ≥ comparison correctly. Based on realistic FMEDA magnitudes from ISO 26262 literature.
known_uncertainty: Exact ISO 26262-5:2018 clause/table numbers (C.3, Table 4) not memorized verbatim; formula SPFM = 1 - Σ(λ_SPF + λ_RF)/Σλ is from ISO 26262-5:2018 and confirmed by multiple secondary sources . ASIL-D target ≥99% is stable across editions .

vector_name: ASIL-D boundary hit — SPFM exactly at 99%
discriminates: Exactly AT the ASIL-D 99% threshold — tests inclusive ≥ semantics. Realistic FMEDA magnitudes. Calculator must return true for ASIL-D (not false due to floating-point <).
known_uncertainty: SPFM formula source: ISO 26262-5:2018 . Threshold inclusivity (≥99%) is the regulatory standard interpretation.

discriminates: Comfortable ASIL-D pass (99.62% >> 99%). Mid-range realistic case with lockstep MCU-class diagnostics. Tests that calculator correctly handles very low SPF/RF fractions without precision underflow.

vector_name: Canonical TI/JESD85 example — 231 units, 1000h, 0 failures, 60% CL

expected_output.interpretation: Upper 60% confidence bound on failure rate is 50.9 FIT

discriminates: Reproduces the canonical TI/JESD85 published example exactly (50.9 FIT) . Tests correct Arrhenius + chi-square formula chaining, 0-failure case (χ²(60%,2) finite), and AF calculation.
known_uncertainty: χ²(60%, 2) = 1.8326 from standard chi-square tables; minor rounding differences across sources. Ea=0.7 eV is the JESD85 COMMON DEFAULT for generic HTOL de-rating, not a universal physical constant for all failure mechanisms .

expected_output.interpretation: Raising confidence level from 60% to 90% raises the FIT upper bound from 50.9 to 126.9 FIT

discriminates: Tests that confidence-level parameter correctly changes χ² quantile and thus the FIT bound. Same physical test, different CL → demonstrates CL sensitivity. Realistic: 90% CL is also commonly reported.
known_uncertainty: χ²(90%, 2) = 4.6052 from standard tables. AF default Ea assumption as noted previously.

expected_output.interpretation: No acceleration (use temp = stress temp); 1 observed failure yields a much higher FIT bound

discriminates: Edge case: AF=1 when T_use = T_stress (no de-rating). Also exercises f=1 (non-zero failures) → χ² df = 4. Tests calculator robustness on degenerate inputs and correct df formula (2f+2).
known_uncertainty: χ²(60%, 4) = 3.2189 from standard tables. The 'AF=1' scenario is physically valid but rarely the primary use case for JESD85 de-rating.

computation: TPP = 2 × MacTOPS × bit_length = 2 × 300 × 8 = 4800. Per EAR 3A090.a (Feb 14, 2025 rule): 3A090.a applies if TPP ≥ 4800 OR (TPP ≥ 1600 AND performance density ≥ 5.92). TPP = 4800 exactly → ≥ 4800 is TRUE → 3A090.a applies.
discriminates: Exact boundary at TPP=4800 — tests inclusive ≥ comparison at the primary 3A090.a threshold. Current regulatory values from Federal Register Vol. 90, No. 30 (Feb 14, 2025) .
known_uncertainty: Thresholds are CURRENT as of the February 14, 2025 Federal Register rule . TPP formula: TPP = 2 × MacTOPS × bit_length, aggregated over all processing units . These values may be revised in future BIS rulemaking.

vector_name: Below TPP=4800 but performance density ≥ 5.92 → 3A090.a via PD path
computation: TPP = 2 × 200 × 8 = 3200. Performance Density (PD) = TPP / die_area = 3200 / 200 = 16.0. Per 3A090.a: TPP ≥ 4800? FALSE (3200 < 4800). BUT (TPP ≥ 1600 AND PD ≥ 5.92)? TRUE (3200 ≥ 1600 AND 16.0 ≥ 5.92). → 3A090.a applies via the PD path.
discriminates: TPP below 4800 but PD path triggers 3A090.a — tests the OR logic of the 3A090.a classification. Uses realistic die area (200 mm² class GPU/accelerator). Demonstrates that PD can pull a sub-4800 TPP chip into 3A090.a.
known_uncertainty: 3A090.a PD threshold = 5.92 is from Feb 14, 2025 Federal Register . 'Applicable die area' definition per BIS may be nuanced for multi-die packages; this vector assumes a single monolithic die.

computation: TPP = 2 × 150 × 8 = 2400. PD = 2400 / 203.05 = 11.82. Wait — recalc: to get PD just below 5.92 with TPP=2400: die_area = 2400 / 5.91 = 406.09 mm². Using die_area = 406.09 mm²: PD = 2400 / 406.09 = 5.909 ≈ 5.91. Per 3A090.b: path (b.1) requires 2400 ≤ TPP < 4800 AND 1.6 ≤ PD < 5.92. TPP=2400 ✓ (≥2400), PD=5.91 ✓ (<5.92). → 3A090.b applies. NOT 3A090.a because PD < 5.92 (so the PD path of 3A090.a fails) and TPP < 4800 (so the TPP path of 3A090.a fails).
discriminates: 3A090.b lower TPP boundary (exactly 2400) and PD just below 5.92 — tests that calculator distinguishes 3A090.a (PD≥5.92) from 3A090.b (PD<5.92) at the same TPP. Critical boundary discrimination per current EAR .
known_uncertainty: 3A090.b thresholds from Feb 14, 2025 Federal Register : 2400 ≤ TPP < 4800 AND 1.6 ≤ PD < 5.92, OR 1600 ≤ TPP AND 3.2 ≤ PD < 5.92. Note: 2400 is INCLUSIVE for 3A090.b.b1 per '2400 or more and less than 4800' .
